question: What knowledge lies beyond the graded knowledges of the means?
premises: There is a knowledge even beyond the previously described levels.
This knowledge is free from means and similar supports.
It rests in the power of bliss and is called unsurpassed.
inference: Beyond all method-based knowledges stands a supreme, unsurpassed knowledge grounded in the power of bliss.
uncertainties: The force of ādi in upāyādi could include more than means alone.
plain_english: Even beyond that is a supreme knowledge, free from means and the like, resting in the power of bliss; here it is called the unsurpassed.
